Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said during the company's fiscal fourth quarter earnings call that a strong labor market was driving the uptick in consumer spending, despite widespread uncertainty. His comments came as Visa posted its highest rate of annual revenue growth in more than 15 years.
Ryan McInerney, Visa Philip Pacheco/Bloomberg - Key insights: Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said that a strong labor market was driving the uptick in consumer spending, despite widespread uncertainty. - What's at stake: The payments giant posted its highest rate of annual revenue growth in more than 15 years. If one were to ask Visa CEO Ryan McInerney what was driving strong consumer spending even in the face of widespread uncertainty, he would point to the labor market. "The foundation underlying [U.S. payment volume growth] more than anything is employment," McInerney said Tuesday during the company's fiscal fourth quarter earnings call with investors. "Anyone in this country who wants a job for the most part has a job, and that strength of employment, despite consumer uncertainty, is delivering … the strength in spending," McInerney said. "We see the resilience across the spending bands on our network. So, we've seen stability in that sense. But in terms of [determining] how strong for how long and what the new normal is, I just think it's too hard to tell." Unemployment has hovered between 4.2% and 4.3% all year, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

ultimate.snippet:
### Visa Announces Leadership Transition
November 17, 2022
*Ryan McInerney, President since 2013, to become CEO effective February 1, 2023*
*Current CEO Alfred F. Kelly, Jr. to become Executive Chairman of the Board after McInerney’s appointment*
SAN FRANCISCO,--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Visa (V: NYSE) today announced the appointment of Ryan McInerney as CEO, effective February 1, 2023. McInerney currently serves as President of Visa, a role he has held since 2013. He will take over as CEO from Alfred F. Kelly, Jr., who has served as the company’s CEO since 2016 and Chairman since 2019. Following McInerney’s appointment, Kelly will assume the role of Executive Chairman of the Board.

In his role as President, McInerney has been responsible for Visa’s global businesses, delivering value to Visa’s financial institutions, acquirers, merchants, and partners in more than 200 countries and territories around the world. He has overseen the company’s market teams, business units, product team, merchant team, and client services. Ryan is a seasoned leader in the payments and consumer banking industry with 20 years of experience delivering solutions to clients.

“I am honored and humbled to become the newest CEO of Visa,” said Ryan McInerney, President. “I want to thank Al for his partnership and mentorship over the past few years and the Board of Directors for its confidence and trust. I am looking forward to continuing to help Visa deliver innovative solutions that help individuals, businesses, and economies thrive.”

# Visa Approves $50 Million Stock Award for CEO Ryan McInerney
[Visa Inc.](https://www.bloomberg.com/quote/V:US) approved a $50 million stock award for Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney as the payments firm seeks to keep a leader who has helped boost its stock 78% during his tenure.
“The award is intended to encourage Mr. McInerney’s long-term retention, reward him based on the execution of the company’s long-term strategy, and further align his interests with the long-term interests of the company’s shareholders,” Visa said in a [filing](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/terminal/TOZ4B9BLKPOG) Monday.
